findings.description: The bucket has no ACL set (defaulting or explicitly noted as public), no server-side encryption configuration, no versioning, and no access logging, exposing sensitive data (customer-master.xlsx) to unauthorized public access and lacking protection against data tampering or loss.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, meaning objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest.
No versioning block is configured, so accidental or malicious deletion/overwrite of objects cannot be recovered, increasing risk from unauthorized modification.
No logging block is configured, preventing detection of unauthorized access attempts to this publicly exposed data bucket.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing customer data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket storing financial data, leaving it unencrypted at rest.
No versioning block configured, risking irrecoverable loss or tampering of financial data.
No logging block configured, preventing audit visibility into access of financial data.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operations data is stored unencrypted.
No logging block configured, preventing audit visibility into access of this bucket.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving data science bucket contents unencrypted at rest.
